subject: general
question: When was Purna Swaraj i.e. complete freedom from the British Raj declared by the Indian National Congress?
solution:
The correct answer is __**26th January 1930**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **26th January 1930** was the day when the Indian National Congress declared Purna Swaraj, or complete freedom from the British Raj.
 
• This declaration was made during the Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress, which was held in December 1929 under the presidency of Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• The Purna Swaraj resolution was a significant milestone in the Indian independence movement, symbolizing the Congress's commitment to full independence rather than dominion status.
 
• Following this declaration, 26th January was celebrated as Independence Day by the Congress party until India achieved actual independence on 15th August 1947.
 
• The significance of the date is also marked by the fact that the Constitution of India came into effect on 26th January 1950, making India a sovereign republic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Lahore Session** of the Indian National Congress in 1929 was a turning point in the Indian freedom struggle, leading to the adoption of the resolution of Purna Swaraj.
 
• On the midnight of 31st December 1929, the tricolor flag was unfurled on the banks of the Ravi River in Lahore.
 
• The Congress appealed to the people of India to observe 26th January as Independence Day by hoisting the national flag and participating in civil disobedience movements.
 
• The demand for complete independence (Purna Swaraj) was a departure from the earlier stance of seeking dominion status within the British Empire.
 
• This resolution galvanized the Indian masses and intensified the struggle for independence, leading to various movements and protests against British rule.
